functions.name: Finance
functions.description: Group finance — close, cash, unit economics. Shared across brands.

responsibilities.title: Hold brand P&L and function heads to plan
Keep C-suite and function heads staffed and scored
Approve sites and capital against return
Design and own the studio operating system — every SOP, process and system a studio network uns on
responsibilities.description: Sets out how every part of a studio works, from the front desk to the sterilisation room, as written procedures and working systems the teams run on daily. Kept current through a regular review cycle, so what audits and complaints reveal changes the standard rather than sitting in a report.

responsibilities.title: Own hygiene and safety across the network — every studio sterile, safe, and run to medical-grade discipline
responsibilities.description: Sets the standards for sterilisation, biomedical waste and safe working, in studios and at headquarters. The bar is written down, trained in, and checked on the same audit cycle as everything else, because in this business one lapse costs more than a year of savings.

responsibilities.title: Own customer feedback and grievances — every complaint, escalation and crisis handled through to resolution
responsibilities.description: Reads satisfaction scores and feedback from every studio, works each complaint and escalation to a close, and runs the crisis response when an incident turns medical, legal or public. What the complaints reveal feeds back into the operating system so the same failure stops repeating; employee matters stay with the people function.

responsibilities.title: Build and run the training department — every studio team trained on the Aliens way of running a studio
responsibilities.description: Sets up the department and the person who leads it daily, and answers for what it produces. Trains new floor staff at joining, refreshes live studio teams, and prepares the teams of newly opened studios; the art itself is taught elsewhere

responsibilities.title: Build and run the studio audit system — checking what every studio delivers against the written standard
responsibilities.description: Designs the complete quality-assurance engine for studio operations: what gets checked, how it is scored, and how often. Sets up the audit team and its lead, and answers for every finding reaching closure. The results feed straight back into training and the operating standard.

responsibilities.title: Coach cluster and studio managers
Deliver studio revenue and merchandise mix
Hold walk-in to close and ATV
NPS and process compliance
Artist utilisation and quality
Deliver cluster revenue and studio hit-rate
Own consultation-to-close and ATV in the cluster
Coach studio managers; hold NPS

kras.name: Hiring Delivery & Ownership

responsibilities.description: Understand hiring requirements from hiring managers.
Prepare a hiring strategy for every open role.
Own the complete recruitment lifecycle from requisition to joining.
Take ownership of hiring targets and hiring outcomes.

executionOutcomes: Role requirements are clearly defined before sourcing begins.
Recruitment plan prepared with sourcing strategy and hiring timelines.
Positions are closed within agreed TAT while maintaining quality.
Hiring goals achieved with minimal escalations.

kras.name: Talent Sourcing & Pipeline Management

responsibilities.description: Source candidates using multiple hiring channels.
Use LinkedIn Recruiter, Boolean Search and advanced sourcing methods.
Develop creative sourcing strategies for difficult roles.
Build and maintain talent pipelines for future hiring.

executionOutcomes: Consistent pipeline of qualified candidates.
Improved sourcing efficiency and better quality candidates.
Hard-to-fill roles closed faster.
Ready database of passive and active candidates.
performanceOutcomes: Maintain minimum 10 qualified candidates in the pipeline for every active position. "

kras.name: Candidate Assessment & Hiring Quality

responsibilities.description: Conduct structured screening interviews.
Evaluate candidates for technical skills, behavioural fit and cultural alignment.
Make objective hiring recommendations supported by evidence.
Communicate interview feedback and hiring decisions professionally.

executionOutcomes: Communication Skills
Able to make decesions
Assessment & Evaluation
Behavioural & Competency-Based Interviewing

kras.name: Candidate Experience & Employer Representation

responsibilities.description: Maintain regular communication with candidates throughout the hiring process.
Ensure every candidate receives a professional recruitment experience.
Build trust and maintain long-term candidate relationships.

executionOutcomes: Lower candidate drop-off rates.
High candidate satisfaction and positive employer branding.
Increased referrals and repeat candidate engagement.

kras.name: Recruitment Operations & Process Excellence

responsibilities.description: Maintain accurate candidate records in Zoho Recruit.
Maintain recruitment trackers and documentation.
Follow recruitment SOPs and workflows consistently.
Review all recruitment documentation before progressing candidates.

executionOutcomes: ATS data accuracy above 95%.
Updated hiring reports with zero missing information.
Standardized recruitment process across all roles.
Reduced recruitment errors.
performanceOutcomes: Ensure 100% interview feedback shared within 48 hours

kras.name: Employer Branding & Talent Attraction

responsibilities.description: Promote Aliens Tattoo as an employer of choice.
Use social media to attract talent.
Create engaging recruitment content and job advertisements internal as a referal system

executionOutcomes: Increase in quality organic applications.
Better sourcing through LinkedIn, Instagram and other platforms.
Higher application conversion rates.

kras.name: Recruitment Innovation & Continuous Improvement

responsibilities.description: Improve recruitment processes and workflows.
Build recruitment trackers, dashboards and reporting tools.
Recommend automation and process improvements.
Introduce innovative sourcing or hiring practices.

executionOutcomes: Faster hiring with fewer process gaps.
Better hiring visibility and decision-making.
Increased operational efficiency.
Better quality hiring and recruiter productivity.

kras.name: Video Production & Shooting

responsibilities.title: Video Production & Shooting
responsibilities.description: Plan and shoot raw footage on location and in-studio per the brief — camera operation, framing, lighting and on-set audio.

executionOutcomes: Operates the camera confidently — exposure, focus, frame rate, lens choice — to get clean, usable footage without hand-holding.
Lights a scene (natural or artificial) to match the brief — key/fill/back and colour temperature.
Frames shots with intent — composition, movement, coverage — so the edit has the angles it needs.
Captures clean location audio (mics, levels, room tone) so post isn't fixing what shouldn't be broken.
Puts people at ease and directs them to natural, on-brief performances during a shoot.
performanceOutcomes: Footage quality — technically clean (focus, exposure, audio) at ingest
First-pass footage acceptance (editor has the coverage the brief needed)

responsibilities.title: Select materials, finishes and furniture. Approve samples and substitutes. Share clear specifications with Procurement and coordinate technical queries with vendors.

executionOutcomes: Support execution until the studio is design-ready. Answer site queries, visit the site, check quality, raise snags and close design issues before opening.

Own design quality and design readiness. Expansion owns site selection, Procurement owns commercials and POs, and the Project Manager owns construction and the overall opening plan.

behaviours.meaning: How well does this person treat their spot on the team as something earned through performance rather than tenure or relationships?

behaviours.name: Dependable under pressure
behaviours.meaning: When stakes are high, deadlines tight, or things going wrong, how does this person respond?

behaviours.name: Problem solvers, not problem delegators
behaviours.meaning: When this person hits a problem outside their direct lane, what do they typically do?

behaviours.name: Impact over effort
behaviours.meaning: Does this person measure their work by outcomes created, or by activity performed?

behaviours.name: Step in when someone drops the ball
behaviours.meaning: When the mission is at risk and someone else has dropped a ball, what does this person do?

behaviours.name: Help each other rise
behaviours.meaning: How actively does this person coach, challenge, and uplift teammates' growth?

behaviours.name: Collaborate to sharpen the mission, not egos
behaviours.meaning: When working across teams or roles, does this person let the best ideas win, or defend their own?

behaviours.name: Chase clarity before action
behaviours.meaning: Before committing to action, does this person invest in defining and aligning on what success looks like?

behaviours.name: Feedback is the fuel to growth
behaviours.meaning: How does this person treat feedback — defensively, passively, or as fuel?

behaviours.name: Benchmark against the best, globally
behaviours.meaning: Whose work does this person measure themselves against — local peers, or global leaders?

behaviours.name: Seek mastery, not just completion
behaviours.meaning: Is this person's standard "done" or "remarkable"?

behaviours.name: Discipline over mood
behaviours.meaning: How consistently does this person deliver regardless of motivation, energy, or personal circumstances?

behaviours.name: Dream big and build bold
behaviours.meaning: When sizing ambition, does this person shrink the vision to fit reality or stretch reality to fit the vision?

behaviours.name: Obsess over craft
behaviours.meaning: How deeply does this person care about the details of their craft — including ones no one else would notice?

behaviours.name: Put in the work, no shortcuts
behaviours.meaning: When given a choice between a faster path and a better path, which does this person take?

behaviours.name: Strive to become irreplaceable
behaviours.meaning: Is this person building distinct value and mastery, or making themselves indispensable through information-hoarding?

behaviours.name: Outgrow ourselves consistently
behaviours.meaning: Does this person treat growth as a daily habit or an annual review item?

behaviours.name: Train for a world-class mindset
behaviours.meaning: Does this person study how the best in the world think and act, and apply those models to their own work?

behaviours.name: Learn to solve big, not to impress
behaviours.meaning: When this person learns something new, does it show up in better outcomes — or in better-sounding conversations?

behaviours.name: Proactive self-learning over handholding
behaviours.meaning: When this person encounters something they don't know, what do they do first?

behaviours.name: Coach to rise together
behaviours.meaning: How actively does this person teach, mentor, and share what they've learned?

behaviours.name: Reflect before we repeat
behaviours.meaning: After a piece of work — win or loss — does this person extract lessons, or just move on?

behaviours.name: Evolve relentlessly
behaviours.meaning: At their current level, is this person still actively pushing into the next?

behaviours.name: Build systems, not one-offs
behaviours.meaning: When this person solves a problem, do they fix it once or design so it never happens again?

behaviours.name: See everything through the lens of process
behaviours.meaning: Does this person create clear, repeatable processes, or rely on memory and personal style?

behaviours.name: Find better ways
behaviours.meaning: Does this person follow processes mechanically, or improve them?

behaviours.name: Take pride in the invisible work
behaviours.meaning: How well does this person handle the backstage work — files, trackers, handoffs, documentation?

behaviours.name: Design the experience, not just the output
behaviours.meaning: Does this person think about how the recipient experiences the work, or just whether the work is done?

behaviours.name: Put Aliens first
behaviours.meaning: When this person's interest, their team's interest, and Aliens' interest are in tension, what wins?

behaviours.name: Conscious with resources
behaviours.meaning: Does this person treat company time, money, and energy as if it were their own?

behaviours.name: Every customer is your customer
behaviours.meaning: How does this person treat customers — as their own, or as "Aliens' customers"?

behaviours.name: Lead with love
behaviours.meaning: In every interaction, does this person leave the other person better than they found them?

behaviours.name: Practice candor with care
behaviours.meaning: How does this person deliver hard truths — with empathy and clarity, or with avoidance, harshness, or sugarcoating?

behaviours.name: Be a go-giver
behaviours.meaning: Does this person give more attention, energy, and generosity than expected — without keeping score?

behaviours.name: Build relationships, not transactions
behaviours.meaning: Does this person invest in trust and connection with people, or treat them as roles?

behaviours.name: Celebrate and support
behaviours.meaning: Does this person show up consistently — for both wins and setbacks?

behaviours.name: Hold each other to greatness
behaviours.meaning: Does this person let mediocrity slide to keep peace, or push others to rise out of care?

behaviours.name: Honesty in word and deed
behaviours.meaning: Does this person tell the truth — even when it's inconvenient, costly, or uncomfortable?

behaviours.name: Keep commitments
behaviours.meaning: When this person says they'll do something, can it be counted on without follow-up?

behaviours.name: Do right when no one is watching
behaviours.meaning: Are this person's standards the same when they're being observed as when they're alone?

behaviours.name: Own mistakes openly
behaviours.meaning: When this person makes a mistake, do they name it quickly or deflect, hide, or blame?

behaviours.name: Not a family, but champions
behaviours.meaning: How well does this person treat their spot on the team as something earned through performance rather than tenure or relationships?

behaviours.name: Dependable under pressure
behaviours.meaning: When stakes are high, deadlines tight, or things going wrong, how does this person respond?

behaviours.name: Problem solvers, not problem delegators
behaviours.meaning: When this person hits a problem outside their direct lane, what do they typically do?

behaviours.name: Impact over effort
behaviours.meaning: Does this person measure their work by outcomes created, or by activity performed?

behaviours.name: Step in when someone drops the ball
behaviours.meaning: When the mission is at risk and someone else has dropped a ball, what does this person do?

behaviours.name: Help each other rise
behaviours.meaning: How actively does this person coach, challenge, and uplift teammates' growth?

behaviours.name: Collaborate to sharpen the mission, not egos
behaviours.meaning: When working across teams or roles, does this person let the best ideas win, or defend their own?

behaviours.name: Chase clarity before action
behaviours.meaning: Before committing to action, does this person invest in defining and aligning on what success looks like?

behaviours.name: Feedback is the fuel to growth
behaviours.meaning: How does this person treat feedback — defensively, passively, or as fuel?

behaviours.name: Benchmark against the best, globally
behaviours.meaning: Whose work does this person measure themselves against — local peers, or global leaders?

behaviours.name: Seek mastery, not just completion
behaviours.meaning: Is this person's standard "done" or "remarkable"?

behaviours.name: Discipline over mood
behaviours.meaning: How consistently does this person deliver regardless of motivation, energy, or personal circumstances?

behaviours.name: Dream big and build bold
behaviours.meaning: When sizing ambition, does this person shrink the vision to fit reality or stretch reality to fit the vision?

behaviours.name: Obsess over craft
behaviours.meaning: How deeply does this person care about the details of their craft — including ones no one else would notice?

behaviours.name: Put in the work, no shortcuts
behaviours.meaning: When given a choice between a faster path and a better path, which does this person take?

behaviours.name: Strive to become irreplaceable
behaviours.meaning: Is this person building distinct value and mastery, or making themselves indispensable through information-hoarding?

behaviours.name: Outgrow ourselves consistently
behaviours.meaning: Does this person treat growth as a daily habit or an annual review item?

behaviours.name: Train for a world-class mindset
behaviours.meaning: Does this person study how the best in the world think and act, and apply those models to their own work?

behaviours.name: Learn to solve big, not to impress
behaviours.meaning: When this person learns something new, does it show up in better outcomes — or in better-sounding conversations?

behaviours.name: Proactive self-learning over handholding
behaviours.meaning: When this person encounters something they don't know, what do they do first?

behaviours.name: Coach to rise together
behaviours.meaning: How actively does this person teach, mentor, and share what they've learned?

behaviours.name: Reflect before we repeat
behaviours.meaning: After a piece of work — win or loss — does this person extract lessons, or just move on?

behaviours.name: Evolve relentlessly
behaviours.meaning: At their current level, is this person still actively pushing into the next?

behaviours.name: Build systems, not one-offs
behaviours.meaning: When this person solves a problem, do they fix it once or design so it never happens again?

behaviours.name: See everything through the lens of process
behaviours.meaning: Does this person create clear, repeatable processes, or rely on memory and personal style?

behaviours.name: Find better ways
behaviours.meaning: Does this person follow processes mechanically, or improve them?

behaviours.name: Take pride in the invisible work
behaviours.meaning: How well does this person handle the backstage work — files, trackers, handoffs, documentation?

behaviours.name: Design the experience, not just the output
behaviours.meaning: Does this person think about how the recipient experiences the work, or just whether the work is done?

behaviours.name: Put Aliens first
behaviours.meaning: When this person's interest, their team's interest, and Aliens' interest are in tension, what wins?

behaviours.name: Conscious with resources
behaviours.meaning: Does this person treat company time, money, and energy as if it were their own?

behaviours.name: Every customer is your customer
behaviours.meaning: How does this person treat customers — as their own, or as "Aliens' customers"?

behaviours.name: Lead with love
behaviours.meaning: In every interaction, does this person leave the other person better than they found them?

behaviours.name: Practice candor with care
behaviours.meaning: How does this person deliver hard truths — with empathy and clarity, or with avoidance, harshness, or sugarcoating?

behaviours.name: Be a go-giver
behaviours.meaning: Does this person give more attention, energy, and generosity than expected — without keeping score?

behaviours.name: Build relationships, not transactions
behaviours.meaning: Does this person invest in trust and connection with people, or treat them as roles?

behaviours.name: Celebrate and support
behaviours.meaning: Does this person show up consistently — for both wins and setbacks?

behaviours.name: Hold each other to greatness
behaviours.meaning: Does this person let mediocrity slide to keep peace, or push others to rise out of care?

behaviours.name: Honesty in word and deed
behaviours.meaning: Does this person tell the truth — even when it's inconvenient, costly, or uncomfortable?

behaviours.name: Keep commitments
behaviours.meaning: When this person says they'll do something, can it be counted on without follow-up?

behaviours.name: Do right when no one is watching
behaviours.meaning: Are this person's standards the same when they're being observed as when they're alone?

behaviours.name: Own mistakes openly
behaviours.meaning: When this person makes a mistake, do they name it quickly or deflect, hide, or blame?

behaviours.meaning: How does this person treat customers — as their own, or as "Aliens' customers"?

behaviours.name: Lead with love
behaviours.meaning: In every interaction, does this person leave the other person better than they found them?

behaviours.name: Practice candor with care
behaviours.meaning: How does this person deliver hard truths — with empathy and clarity, or with avoidance, harshness, or sugarcoating?

behaviours.name: Be a go-giver
behaviours.meaning: Does this person give more attention, energy, and generosity than expected — without keeping score?

behaviours.name: Build relationships, not transactions
behaviours.meaning: Does this person invest in trust and connection with people, or treat them as roles?

behaviours.name: Celebrate and support
behaviours.meaning: Does this person show up consistently — for both wins and setbacks?

behaviours.name: Hold each other to greatness
behaviours.meaning: Does this person let mediocrity slide to keep peace, or push others to rise out of care?

behaviours.name: Honesty in word and deed
behaviours.meaning: Does this person tell the truth — even when it's inconvenient, costly, or uncomfortable?

behaviours.name: Keep commitments
behaviours.meaning: When this person says they'll do something, can it be counted on without follow-up?

behaviours.name: Do right when no one is watching
behaviours.meaning: Are this person's standards the same when they're being observed as when they're alone?

behaviours.name: Own mistakes openly
behaviours.meaning: When this person makes a mistake, do they name it quickly or deflect, hide, or blame?

behaviours.name: Coach to rise together

behaviours.name: Reflect before we repeat

behaviours.name: Evolve relentlessly

behaviours.name: Build systems, not one-offs
behaviours.meaning: When this person solves a problem, do they fix it once or design so it never happens again?

behaviours.name: See everything through the lens of process

behaviours.name: Find better ways

behaviours.name: Take pride in the invisible work

behaviours.name: Design the experience, not just the output

behaviours.name: Put Aliens first

behaviours.name: Conscious with resources

behaviours.name: Every customer is your customer

behaviours.name: Lead with love

behaviours.name: Practice candor with care

behaviours.name: Be a go-giver

behaviours.name: Build relationships, not transactions

behaviours.name: Celebrate and support
behaviours.meaning: Does this person show up consistently — for both wins and setbacks?

behaviours.name: Hold each other to greatness

behaviours.name: Honesty in word and deed

behaviours.name: Keep commitments

behaviours.name: Build relationships, not transactions
behaviours.meaning: Does this person invest in trust and connection with people, or treat them as roles?

behaviours.name: Celebrate and support
behaviours.meaning: Does this person show up consistently — for both wins and setbacks?

behaviours.name: Hold each other to greatness
behaviours.meaning: Does this person let mediocrity slide to keep peace, or push others to rise out of care?

behaviours.name: Honesty in word and deed
behaviours.meaning: Does this person tell the truth — even when it's inconvenient, costly, or uncomfortable?

behaviours.name: Keep commitments
behaviours.meaning: When this person says they'll do something, can it be counted on without follow-up?

behaviours.name: Do right when no one is watching
behaviours.meaning: Are this person's standards the same when they're being observed as when they're alone?

behaviours.name: Own mistakes openly
behaviours.meaning: When this person makes a mistake, do they name it quickly or deflect, hide, or blame?

behaviours.meaning: How well does this person treat their spot on the team as something earned through performance rather than tenure or relationships?

behaviours.name: Dependable under pressure

behaviours.name: Problem solvers, not problem delegators
behaviours.meaning: When this person hits a problem outside their direct lane, what do they typically do?

behaviours.name: Impact over effort
behaviours.meaning: Does this person measure their work by outcomes created, or by activity performed?

behaviours.name: Step in when someone drops the ball
behaviours.meaning: When the mission is at risk and someone else has dropped a ball, what does this person do?

behaviours.name: Help each other rise
behaviours.meaning: How actively does this person coach, challenge, and uplift teammates' growth?

behaviours.name: Collaborate to sharpen the mission, not egos
behaviours.meaning: When working across teams or roles, does this person let the best ideas win, or defend their own?

behaviours.name: Chase clarity before action

behaviours.name: Feedback is the fuel to growth
behaviours.meaning: How does this person treat feedback — defensively, passively, or as fuel?

behaviours.name: Benchmark against the best, globally

behaviours.name: Seek mastery, not just completion
behaviours.meaning: Is this person's standard "done" or "remarkable"?

behaviours.name: Discipline over mood
behaviours.meaning: How consistently does this person deliver regardless of motivation, energy, or personal circumstances?

behaviours.name: Dream big and build bold
behaviours.meaning: When sizing ambition, does this person shrink the vision to fit reality or stretch reality to fit the vision?

behaviours.name: Obsess over craft

behaviours.name: Put in the work, no shortcuts
behaviours.meaning: When given a choice between a faster path and a better path, which does this person take?

behaviours.name: Outgrow ourselves consistently
behaviours.meaning: Does this person treat growth as a daily habit or an annual review item?

behaviours.name: Find better ways

behaviours.name: Be a go-giver

behaviours.name: Build relationships, not transactions

behaviours.name: Celebrate and support

behaviours.name: Hold each other to greatness

behaviours.meaning: When this person learns something new, does it show up in better outcomes — or in better-sounding conversations?

behaviours.name: Proactive self-learning over handholding
behaviours.meaning: When this person encounters something they don't know, what do they do first?

behaviours.name: Coach to rise together
behaviours.meaning: How actively does this person teach, mentor, and share what they've learned?

behaviours.name: Reflect before we repeat
behaviours.meaning: After a piece of work — win or loss — does this person extract lessons, or just move on?

behaviours.name: Evolve relentlessly
behaviours.meaning: At their current level, is this person still actively pushing into the next?

behaviours.name: Build systems, not one-offs
behaviours.meaning: When this person solves a problem, do they fix it once or design so it never happens again?

behaviours.name: See everything through the lens of process
behaviours.meaning: Does this person create clear, repeatable processes, or rely on memory and personal style?

behaviours.name: Find better ways
behaviours.meaning: Does this person follow processes mechanically, or improve them?

behaviours.name: Take pride in the invisible work
behaviours.meaning: How well does this person handle the backstage work — files, trackers, handoffs, documentation?

behaviours.name: Design the experience, not just the output
behaviours.meaning: Does this person think about how the recipient experiences the work, or just whether the work is done?

behaviours.name: Put Aliens first
behaviours.meaning: When this person's interest, their team's interest, and Aliens' interest are in tension, what wins?

behaviours.name: Conscious with resources
behaviours.meaning: Does this person treat company time, money, and energy as if it were their own?

behaviours.name: Every customer is your customer
behaviours.meaning: How does this person treat customers — as their own, or as "Aliens' customers"?

behaviours.name: Lead with love
behaviours.meaning: In every interaction, does this person leave the other person better than they found them?

behaviours.name: Practice candor with care
behaviours.meaning: How does this person deliver hard truths — with empathy and clarity, or with avoidance, harshness, or sugarcoating?

behaviours.name: Be a go-giver
behaviours.meaning: Does this person give more attention, energy, and generosity than expected — without keeping score?

behaviours.name: Build relationships, not transactions
behaviours.meaning: Does this person invest in trust and connection with people, or treat them as roles?

behaviours.name: Celebrate and support
behaviours.meaning: Does this person show up consistently — for both wins and setbacks?

behaviours.name: Hold each other to greatness
behaviours.meaning: Does this person let mediocrity slide to keep peace, or push others to rise out of care?

behaviours.name: Honesty in word and deed
behaviours.meaning: Does this person tell the truth — even when it's inconvenient, costly, or uncomfortable?

behaviours.name: Keep commitments
behaviours.meaning: When this person says they'll do something, can it be counted on without follow-up?

behaviours.name: Do right when no one is watching
behaviours.meaning: Are this person's standards the same when they're being observed as when they're alone?

behaviours.name: Own mistakes openly
behaviours.meaning: When this person makes a mistake, do they name it quickly or deflect, hide, or blame?

behaviours.name: Not a family, but champions
behaviours.meaning: How well does this person treat their spot on the team as something earned through performance rather than tenure or relationships?

behaviours.name: Dependable under pressure
behaviours.meaning: When stakes are high, deadlines tight, or things going wrong, how does this person respond?

behaviours.name: Problem solvers, not problem delegators
behaviours.meaning: When this person hits a problem outside their direct lane, what do they typically do?

behaviours.name: Impact over effort
behaviours.meaning: Does this person measure their work by outcomes created, or by activity performed?

behaviours.name: Step in when someone drops the ball
behaviours.meaning: When the mission is at risk and someone else has dropped a ball, what does this person do?

behaviours.name: Help each other rise
behaviours.meaning: How actively does this person coach, challenge, and uplift teammates' growth?

behaviours.name: Collaborate to sharpen the mission, not egos
behaviours.meaning: When working across teams or roles, does this person let the best ideas win, or defend their own?

behaviours.name: Chase clarity before action
behaviours.meaning: Before committing to action, does this person invest in defining and aligning on what success looks like?

behaviours.name: Feedback is the fuel to growth
behaviours.meaning: How does this person treat feedback — defensively, passively, or as fuel?

behaviours.name: Benchmark against the best, globally
behaviours.meaning: Whose work does this person measure themselves against — local peers, or global leaders?

behaviours.name: Seek mastery, not just completion
behaviours.meaning: Is this person's standard "done" or "remarkable"?

behaviours.name: Discipline over mood
behaviours.meaning: How consistently does this person deliver regardless of motivation, energy, or personal circumstances?

behaviours.name: Dream big and build bold
behaviours.meaning: When sizing ambition, does this person shrink the vision to fit reality or stretch reality to fit the vision?

behaviours.name: Obsess over craft
behaviours.meaning: How deeply does this person care about the details of their craft — including ones no one else would notice?

behaviours.name: Put in the work, no shortcuts
behaviours.meaning: When given a choice between a faster path and a better path, which does this person take?

behaviours.name: Strive to become irreplaceable
behaviours.meaning: Is this person building distinct value and mastery, or making themselves indispensable through information-hoarding?

behaviours.name: Outgrow ourselves consistently
behaviours.meaning: Does this person treat growth as a daily habit or an annual review item?
